title: How do monetary incentives affect prosocial behavior among gig workers?—Behavioral experiments based on FlashEx
abstract: The gig economy has reshaped labor markets. Motivating mobile, loosely contracted gig workers to engage in prosocial behavior is critical for platform governance. This paper uses a randomized field experiment on FlashEx in comparable Chinese cities to examine how monetary incentives affect delivery workers’ prosocial behavior and related economic outcomes. The main findings of this study are as follows. First, monetary incentives significantly promote gig workers’ prosocial behavior, effectively increasing both the likelihood and frequency of their participation in altruistic acts. This effect is primarily driven by the “instrumental value” mechanism in the gig economy: the platform’s gold coin rewards, accompanied by privileges such as priority order allocation, enable prosocial behavior to be converted into a critical resource for improving productivity and income, thereby avoiding the “signal contamination” often associated with traditional monetary incentives. In addition, as an institutional signal, gold coin rewards transform prosocial behavior from spontaneous altruism into a form of identity construction and institutional recognition within the platform ecosystem, enhancing the professional sustainability of such behavior. Second, the effectiveness of monetary incentives exhibits significant heterogeneity across different groups of gig workers. The heterogeneity analysis shows that the incentive mechanism is more effective for highly engaged “quasi-full-time” workers and those with pre-existing prosocial tendencies, reflecting a complementary synergy between external incentives and intrinsic altruistic motivation. However, for the workers with already outstanding historical performance, the marginal effect of gold coin incentives diminishes, displaying a clear pattern of “high-performer saturation”. At the same time, extreme weather conditions significantly weaken the positive effect of monetary incentives. Third, prosocial behavior incentive policies significantly enhance the work value of gig workers on the platform. Empirical results indicate that implementing such policies can increase gig workers’ cumulative order value by approximately 10.8%. This value enhancement is realized through a mechanism combining monetary incentives and market recognition: prosocial behavior improves user experience, while user-side tipping and ratings further amplify the positive effects of the incentive policy, achieving a synergistic increase in both social and economic value. Overall, this research provides scientific evidence for platform firms to design more targeted management and incentive strategies for gig workers.

title: Costly Prosociality, Familiarity Among Peers, and School Climate: A Predictive Model.
abstract: The objective of this study is to examine the associations between costly prosociality toward known and unknown school peers and well-being, school aggression, and school climate among Chilean secondary school students by estimating structural paths from costly prosociality to these variables. A correlational and explanatory quantitative study was conducted using a sample of 529 Chilean secondary school students recruited through convenience sampling. Likert-type self-report scales were administered to measure costly prosociality, school aggression, well-being, and school climate. HCPB toward both known and unknown peers was positively associated with well-being and school climate. In the structural models, the model involving known peers showed a significant negative path to school aggression, whereas the model involving unknown peers did not show a significant path to school aggression. The two structural models showed different descriptive patterns of associations, with the model involving unknown peers accounting for 34% of the variance in school climate, while the model involving known peers accounted for 27%. These findings provide descriptive evidence of distinct patterns of associations between costly prosociality and school-related variables according to beneficiary familiarity. In the discussion section, results are analyzed in light of the literature.

title: Maternal Avoidant and Anxious/Ambivalent Attachment and Children's Anxiety-Withdrawal: The Serial Indirect Associations of Parental Technoference and Prosocial Behavior.
abstract: Family-related factors play an important role in children's socio-emotional adjustment during early childhood. Although maternal insecure attachment has been consistently associated with parenting processes and children's socio-emotional development, the mechanisms through which these attachment styles are associated with children's anxiety-withdrawal remain insufficiently understood. Parental technoference and children's prosocial behavior have been identified as potential mechanisms underlying this association; however, studies examining these variables within an integrated model are limited. This study was conducted to examine the significant serial indirect association of parental technoference and prosocial behavior in the associations between maternal avoidant and anxious/ambivalent attachment and anxiety-withdrawal among preschool children. To test the proposed associations, a mediation model based on structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed. The study sample comprised 608 preschool children attending independent public preschools in the central districts of Denizli, Türkiye, and their parents. Of the participating children, 356 (58.6%) were girls and 252 (41.4%) were boys, ranging in age from 60 to 72 months. The findings indicated that parental technoference and children's prosocial behavior serially mediated the associations between maternal avoidant and anxious/ambivalent attachment and children's anxiety-withdrawal. The findings further suggest that reducing parental technoference and fostering children's prosocial behavior may be relevant to understanding the association between maternal avoidant and anxious/ambivalent attachment and children's anxiety-withdrawal.

title: Beyond General Prosocial Behavior: Nature Connectedness, Authenticity, and Instrumental Prosocial Behavior in Late Childhood.
abstract: Research linking nature connectedness to prosociality has rarely distinguished motivationally specific forms of helping. The present study examined the associations of nature connectedness with general prosocial behavior and the more specific instrumental prosocial behavior during late childhood, with authenticity examined as an associational variable. Using a cross-sectional design, the final analytic sample comprised 281 Grade 4 and Grade 5 students aged 9-12 years who were recruited through convenience sampling from two primary schools in Yantai, China. Path analyses using factor scores adjusted for differential item functioning were interpreted within an Associational Variable Analysis framework. Nature connectedness was positively associated with authenticity and general prosocial behavior, with a significant positive indirect association involving authenticity. In contrast, authenticity was negatively associated with instrumental prosocial behavior. Nature connectedness showed a positive direct association with instrumental prosocial behavior after accounting for authenticity but a negative indirect association involving authenticity, resulting in a nonsignificant total association. The positive direct association differed by sex and was significant among boys but not girls. These findings underscore the importance of distinguishing instrumental from general prosocial behavior and suggest that authenticity may help differentiate their associations with nature connectedness in late childhood.

title: The Emerging Phenotype of HFpEF in Cardiac Allografts: A Review of Pathophysiology, Diagnosis, and Management.
abstract: Advances in donor selection, organ preservation technologies, donation after circulatory death, and broader geographic sharing have expanded access to heart transplantation but have also introduced new challenges that affect allograft function. The transplanted heart is exposed to multiple insults, including donor brain death, ischemia-reperfusion injury, acute and chronic rejection, and cardiac allograft vasculopathy. Increasingly, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is being recognized as a distinct manifestation of cardiac allograft dysfunction that may contribute to late graft failure. Diastolic dysfunction occurs frequently after heart transplantation and may develop early as a consequence of ischemia-reperfusion injury, primary graft dysfunction, and/or rejection. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy, chronic immune-mediated injury, metabolic comorbidities, and aging of the donor heart further contribute to the HFpEF phenotype. Although the process is multifactorial and can be variable, progressive abnormalities in myocardial relaxation, compliance, microvascular function, and extracellular matrix remodeling may lead to restrictive physiology and then the clinical syndrome of heart failure with low cardiac output and end-organ dysfunction despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. However, the epidemiology, diagnostic criteria, and natural history of HFpEF in transplant recipients remain incompletely characterized. As a result, the goal of this paper is to consolidate the current understanding of the pathophysiology, epidemiology, diagnostic evaluation, and management of HFpEF in cardiac allografts, while identifying current gaps in understanding to guide future research.

title: How physical activity relates to college students’ prosocial behavior through psychological capital and social connectedness
abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of accumulating psychological stress and challenges in social adaptation, physical activity is widely recognized as an important daily behavior associated with the physical and mental health of college students. However, the pathways linking physical activity to prosocial behavior remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study develops a resource transformation framework incorporating physical activity, psychological capital, social connectedness, and prosocial behavior, and examines their differentiated relational pathways in the accumulation of psychological and social resources. Using survey data from 1244 college students, partial least squares structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis were combined to examine the relationships among physical activity, psychological capital, social connectedness, and prosocial behavior. The results indicated no significant direct relationship between physical activity and prosocial behavior. However, significant indirect relationships were identified through psychological capital and social connectedness separately, as well as through the sequential pathway from psychological capital to social connectedness. Necessary condition analysis further indicated that psychological capital was identified as a necessary condition for achieving higher levels of social connectedness, while physical activity, psychological capital, and social connectedness were all identified as necessary conditions for achieving higher levels of prosocial behavior. Theoretically, this study extends the understanding of physical activity from an outcome-oriented health behavior perspective to a resource perspective on the development of social behavior, broadens the explanatory scope of conservation of resources theory in prosocial behavior research, and further elucidates the potential sequential association between psychological and social resources. Practically, the findings provide resource-oriented insights into the use of physical activity to support social adaptation and the development of prosocial behavior among college students, with implications for college physical education and public health practice.

title: Holistic co-design of fibre-optic distributed acoustic sensing and coherent communication.
abstract: Integrating sensing into communication is crucial for the fully-connected and intelligent development of modern life. However, existing fiber-optic sensing and communication systems merely coexist without inadequate resource sharing, resulting in limited scalability for large-scale deployment. Here, we propose a holistically co-designed sensing and communication (CSAC) framework that incorporates multi-level optimization: (i) a dual-function pilot signal that shares time and spectrum resources; (ii) a simplified system using a single transmitter to simultaneously generate multi-tone pilot and subcarrier communication signals; (iii) a point-to-multipoint (P2MP) network that distributes pilot signals for multi-user frequency synchronization and enhanced acoustic sensing response. Our approach achieves multi-point frequency synchronization with an accuracy of 1.56 MHz and enhances acoustic sensing response to 12 kHz. By introducing the on-chip modulators to generate multi-frequency optical comb, the response bandwidth is further expanded to 28 kHz. This CSAC framework efficiently supports dense communication and diverse sensing, offering an eco-sustainable solution for the future optical networks.

title: Classifier-Derived Guidance for Diffusion-Based Medical Dataset Distillation.
abstract: Medical image analysis often relies on large annotated datasets, whose collection, storage, and sharing are costly and constrained by privacy concerns. Dataset distillation offers a potential solution by constructing compact synthetic datasets that retain task-relevant information from the original data. However, generative distillation methods may not adequately preserve class-specific information in medical images, where clinically distinct classes often exhibit similar visual characteristics. To address this issue, we propose a classifier-derived guidance framework for diffusion-based medical dataset distillation. The framework uses predictions from a pretrained noise-conditioned classifier to guide diffusion sampling through three objectives. Classifier guidance (CG) promotes class alignment, whereas entropy and margin guidance encourage boundary-oriented sampling. We analyze guidance-strength sensitivity on three medical imaging datasets across images-per-class (IPC) budgets and evaluate validation-selected COVID-19 Radiography configurations on the test subset using three downstream architectures. Classifier diagnostics distinguish prediction-conditioning agreement from downstream utility, while learning curves illustrate differences in validation behavior despite low training loss. These findings characterize the configuration-dependent utility of classifier-derived guidance for compact synthetic medical datasets.

title: Botulinum toxin type a within function-oriented management of post-stroke spasticity: a narrative review.
abstract: Post-stroke spasticity (PSS) is a heterogeneous complication of stroke that affects motor recovery, care needs, pain, positioning, and participation in daily life. Current management frameworks commonly stratify patients by time since stroke, but disease duration alone does not capture differences in neural mechanisms, residual voluntary control, functional priorities, or response to intervention. This narrative review searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Wanfang databases from inception to May 2026, prioritizing randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, systematic reviews, real-world studies, Goal Attainment Scaling research, the Upper Limb International Spasticity cohort series, best-practice guidance, and clinical trials including BEST and InTENSE. We synthesize evidence that PSS heterogeneity can be understood across central and peripheral mechanisms, temporal trajectories, and active versus passive functional consequences. Available studies suggest that active and passive functional goals differ in baseline functional profiles, outcome assessment, treatment response, and intervention requirements. However, patients sharing a functional goal type may still differ in residual voluntary control, neural and non-neural contributors to movement restriction, pain, mobility, and care dependency. Botulinum toxin type A is well aligned with focal tone reduction and passive goals, including pain relief, hygiene, and limb positioning. It may also support contracture-prevention strategies when modifiable neural muscle overactivity remains, whereas active functional gains usually require preserved motor potential and integration with task-oriented training, rehabilitation, and adjunctive modalities. We propose that functional goal type should complement time-based staging as a decision dimension rather than serve as a complete clinical phenotype. This combined framework may better align patient selection, intervention matching, outcome assessment, and longitudinal treatment planning. Prospective goal-stratified studies and standardized assessment tools are needed to test its clinical utility.

title: Simulating Cooperative Prosocial Behavior with Multi-Agent LLMs: Evidence and Mechanisms for AI Agents to Inform Policy Decisions
abstract: Human prosocial cooperation is essential for our collective health, education, and welfare. However, designing social systems to maintain or incentivize prosocial behavior is challenging because people can act selfishly to maximize personal gain. This complex and unpredictable aspect of human behavior makes it difficult for policymakers to foresee the implications of their designs. Recently, multi-agent LLM systems have shown remarkable capabilities in simulating human-like behavior, and replicating some human lab experiments. This paper studies how well multi-agent systems can simulate prosocial human behavior, such as that seen in the public goods game (PGG), and whether multi-agent systems can exhibit ``unbounded actions'' seen outside the lab in real world scenarios. We find that multi-agent LLM systems successfully replicate human behavior from lab experiments of the public goods game with three experimental treatments - priming, transparency, and varying endowments. Beyond replicating existing experiments, we find that multi-agent LLM systems can replicate the expected human behavior when combining experimental treatments, even if no previous study combined those specific treatments. Lastly, we find that multi-agent systems can exhibit a rich set of unbounded actions that people do in the real world outside of the lab -- such as collaborating and even cheating. In sum, these studies are steps towards a future where LLMs can be used to inform policy decisions that encourage people to act in a prosocial manner.

title: Fear conditioning research through the lens of meta-analyses: A systematic methodological review.
abstract: Meta-analyses have become foundational tools for evidence synthesis and are receiving increasing attention across research disciplines, including fear conditioning - a central paradigm in affective, behavioral, and clinical neuroscience and psychology - where the number of meta-analyses has notably increased in recent years. However, substantial methodological heterogeneity among these meta-analyses complicates their interpretation and comparability. This review systematically summarizes existing meta-analyses in fear conditioning (n = 26), with particular emphasis on methodological choices and reporting standards. Our findings indicate substantial variability in reporting practices, particularly regarding review processes, applied methodological models, and the operationalization of certain variables, which may challenge reproducibility and interpretability. Most meta-analyses used aggregate data and random-effects models, while moderator analyses were frequently conducted but yielded few significant moderators. Outcome measures were frequently aggregated (e.g., skin conductance, startle responses, ratings) without a clear theoretical rationale. We discuss the implications of moderator analyses, the limited attention to temporal dynamics, and the aggregation of diverse outcome measures. We argue that the field would benefit from more precise reporting, theory-driven analytical decisions, and increased data sharing at both the primary and meta-analytic levels. Such improvements would facilitate individual participant data meta-analyses, which preserve within-study variability, enhance moderator analyses, and address challenges inherent to aggregate-level data synthesis. Establishing and expanding shared infrastructures represents a necessary step toward cumulative, reproducible, and clinically informative work in the future.

title: Inter-individual gene expression variability implies stable regulation of brain-biased genes across organs in three ray-finned fishes.
abstract: Phenotypic variation among individuals provides the raw material for evolution, and gene expression is a key mediator between genetic and phenotypic variation. As for phenotypes, the range of gene expression is limited and biased by evolutionary and developmental constraints. Observed expression variability due to biomolecular stochasticity and cell-to-cell heterogeneity has been well-studied in isogenic populations of unicellular organisms. However, for multicellular organisms with a diversity of cells and tissues sharing the same genetic background, the interplay between expression variability, gene and organ function, and gene regulation remains an open question. Here, we use highly multiplexed 3'-end bulk RNA sequencing to generate transcriptome profiles spanning at least nine organs in outbred individuals of three ray-finned fish species: zebrafish, Northern pike, and spotted gar. Per organ, we quantify individual-to-individual gene expression variability independent of mean expression level. Lowly variable genes are enriched in cellular housekeeping functions whereas highly variable genes are enriched in stimulus-response functions. Furthermore, highly variable genes evolve under weaker purifying selection at the protein-coding sequence, indicating that intra-species expression variability predicts inter-species protein sequence divergence. Genes that are broadly expressed across organs are both highly expressed and lowly variable, whereas organ-biased genes are typically highly variable within their top organ. Among organ-biased genes, patterns of expression variance are dependent on the top organ. Specifically, brain- and gonads-biased genes have lowly variable expression across different organs, suggesting stabilizing selection. These patterns suggest that gene regulatory mechanisms evolve under organ-specific selective pressures.

title: Dictators and Lying Dictators: An Experimental Investigation of Preference Based-Group Biases in Chinese and American Interactions
abstract: This study examines group-conditional generosity and behavior using students from Chapman University in the United States and Wuhan University in China. Participants make allocation decisions in either a standard Dictator Game (DG) or a Lying Dictator Game (LDG), where a privately reported die roll determines the allocation. We vary whether participants interact with members of their own or the other university community. The LDG game, through the possibility of plausible deniability, allows for the moderation of image concerns that potentially influence DG behavior. We complement these tasks with individual decision benchmarks that exclude the Receiver to control for group differences in lying aversion. We find no evidence of in-group favoritism in either the DG or LDG, although Chapman participants allocate more to in-group Receivers than do Wuhan participants. Plausible deniability changes allocation distributions, but not in the predicted direction of lower generosity. The individual decision tasks show that private reporting behavior differs across the two samples and that introducing a Receiver shifts behavior in an other-regarding direction.

title: MTC-TCN-Attn: A TCN-Attention-Based Multi-Task Collaborative Prediction Method for Wheat Soil Moisture.
abstract: Wheat is one of the most important staple crops worldwide, and soil moisture plays a critical role in regulating crop growth, irrigation management, and agricultural water-use efficiency. Accurate soil moisture prediction is therefore essential for precision agriculture and intelligent irrigation scheduling. However, soil moisture variations are driven by complex interactions among meteorological conditions, soil layers, and temporal dynamics, resulting in strong nonlinear characteristics and long-term dependencies that remain challenging for conventional prediction approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi-Task Collaborative Temporal Convolutional Network with Attention (MTC-TCN-Attn) model for multi-variable wheat soil moisture prediction. The proposed framework integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with a multi-head self-attention mechanism, where causal and dilated convolutions are employed to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies, while the attention module adaptively identifies informative time steps and enhances global temporal feature representation. Furthermore, a multi-task collaborative learning strategy based on shared feature representations is developed to exploit the intrinsic correlations among multiple soil-moisture-related variables and improve model generalization. Experiments conducted on wheat field data demonstrate that the proposed MTC-TCN-Attn model outperforms representative benchmark models, including SVR, LSTM, Transformer, and Multi-Task Long Short-Term Memory (MT-LSTM), across all five prediction targets in terms of R2, RMSE, and MAE. For the three principal soil-moisture-state variables, the proposed model achieved R2 values of 0.9147, 0.9651, and 0.9622 for surface soil moisture (SSM), subsurface soil moisture (SUSM), and soil moisture profile (SMP), respectively. Compared with single-task and multi-task TCN baselines, the proposed MTC-TCN-Attn model consistently reduces prediction errors and improves robustness by effectively integrating temporal dependency modeling and cross-task information sharing. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for multi-variable soil moisture forecasting and has promising potential for intelligent irrigation management and precision agricultural applications.

title: BMA-Net: A Bilateral Attention Network with Retinal Domain Transfer-Learning for CIMT-Based Cardiovascular Risk Classification from Fundus Images.
abstract: Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) is an established marker of subclinical atherosclerosis, but its reliance on ultrasound equipment and trained operators limits its suitability for large-scale screening. Retinal fundus photography may offer a more scalable approach to vascular assessment, as it contains retinal vascular features associated with systemic cardiovascular health and can be acquired quickly and non-invasively. This study proposes a two-stage transfer learning framework for CIMT-based cardiovascular risk classification. An attention-enhanced EfficientNet-B4 is first pretrained on the Asia Pacific Tele-Ophthalmology Society 2019 Blindness Detection dataset and subsequently transferred to a weight-sharing Siamese architecture to classify the China Fundus Carotid Intima-Media Thickness dataset. Across ten independent initializations, the proposed model achieved an average macro-F1 score of 77.81% and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 84.08% on the validation set and 78.29% and 85.22%, respectively, on the test set. It achieved overall higher point estimates for performance metrics than those previously reported for the Siamese ResNeXt baseline model with squeeze-and-excitation attention, and demonstrated a reduced disparity in class-wise performance. Grad-CAM analysis further revealed differences in the spatial activation patterns between models trained under different experimental configurations. Overall, these findings support the feasibility of fundus imaging as a scalable and non-invasive approach to CIMT-based cardiovascular risk assessment.

title: [A multi-scale attention and federated learning-based method for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 immunohistochemical grading of breast cancer].
abstract: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) images for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) in breast cancer face challenges in cross-institutional sharing and suffer from insufficient representation of boundary categories. To address these issues, this paper proposes an automatic grading method that integrates multi-scale attention mechanisms with federated learning. Specifically, we construct a multi-scale attention residual network 50 (MSA-ResNet50) model, which enhances the model's discriminative capability for membrane staining intensity, staining continuity, and tissue morphological structures by fusing channel attention, spatial attention, and global attention branches in parallel. For the federated learning strategy, we incorporate client-side validation set accuracy and macro-averaged F1 score to perform quality-weighted aggregation based on the federated averaging (FedAvg) algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 87.78%, outperforming comparative methods. Furthermore, visualization results indicate that our model effectively strengthens feature responses in membrane staining regions that are critical for HER2 grading discrimination, thereby improving classification accuracy for the HER2 2+ category, which is clinically challenging to interpret. This work provides a technical reference for subsequent validation on real-world multi-center clinical data.

title: "We built it grassroots… birth by birth": circumpolar maternal child health workshop proceedings.
abstract: Maternity care across the Circumpolar North continues to be shaped by colonial policies, centralized healthcare structures, and the ongoing evacuation of pregnant people from their communities for birth. While these challenges are well documented, less attention has been given to the strengths, innovations, and community-led approaches emerging across Arctic regions. Building on previous engagements of the Circumpolar Maternal and Child Health Working Group, a two-day workshop was convened in Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada, in March 2026. The workshop brought together Elders, Indigenous and non-Indigenous midwives, birthworkers, healthcare providers, researchers, and students from the Circumpolar North to facilitate knowledge exchange and identify lessons from successful community-led birthing initiatives. Grounded in Indigenous knowledge-sharing approaches, the workshop incorporated storytelling, talking circles, small-group discussions, and case study presentations from the Inuulitsivik Midwifery Program and the Fort Smith Midwifery Program. title: Unselfish incentive schemes : a tool to influence peoples' preferences in adoption and diffusion processes
abstract: It is in the interest of many different types of organisations to encourage the adoption of specific products or desirable behaviours. Such goal has been commonly pursued by offering economic incentives to people with the aim of making the desired action more appealing. This type of strategy is based on standard economic theory, which assumes that people behave in ways that maximise only their own economic benefits. However, behavioural scientists have suggested that people frequently make decisions that go against their own benefit and are affected by emotions, biases and social preferences, all of which may lead to the failure of traditional economic incentives. In the present work, prosocial motives are incorporated into the design of incentive schemes by allowing participants to give away part of their rewards to relevant peers. We tested whether such strategy can outperform the traditional “selfish schemes”. Specifically, four experiments using hypothetical scenarios were performed, in which participants’ preferences were elicited by implementing different methodologies. The main variables considered in this research are the number of recipients and the expectations about their reactions, the possibilities of reciprocity, the certainty of the reward, the size and framing of the reward, and the fear of negative evaluations. The results show a substantial proportion of the participants favouring the “unselfish” incentive schemes. Moreover, the expectations about recipients’ reactions were particularly relevant in defining the effectiveness of programmes that incorporate prosocial motives. Findings also suggest that fulfilling others’ expectations allows people to strengthen their self-concept and maintain a positive self-image. This research brings a new perspective in the study of adoption and diffusion processes by incorporating insights and methods from behavioural science, and it considers the role of contextual factors in decision-making processes that have been neglected in the literature. These results can also contribute to the understanding of the mechanisms driving prosocial behaviours and inform the design of initiatives that aim to encourage desirable actions.

title: Language and economic decisions
abstract: Many economic problems are framed using language. We introduce a language-based utility function to rationalize how linguistic framing shapes decision-making. We derive a prediction in the dictator game and empirically test it across 107 experimental instructions. Language is evaluated using deep learning and human methods: BERT, MoralBERT, GPT, and experimental subjects. Among these, GPT evaluations best predict giving behavior. We then examine the mechanism underlying this effect, showing that moral, rather than emotional, evaluations account for the observed patterns. Finally, we assess robustness by deriving predictions in equity–efficiency trade-off, ultimatum, and corruption games, and by showing that GPT evaluations predict human behavior also in these contexts. Our results show that language is a quantifiable dimension of economic decision-making.

title: Facilitators and barriers to health promotion interventions in the National Defence Forces of Ethiopia: a grounded theory study.
abstract: The Ethiopian military implements health promotion interventions to improve and maintain fitness, health, and military readiness. However, distinct organizational features of military forces can affect the health of their members. This study aimed to explore facilitators and barriers to implementing health promotion interventions within Ethiopian military settings and develop a conceptual model based on the findings. A grounded theory approach was used in this qualitative study. We identified 26 participants among health experts engaged in health promotion and disease prevention interventions in Ethiopian military health facilities and health departments. Data were collected using face-to-face interviews with key open questions, which were recorded, transcribed verbatim in Amharic, and translated into English. The English transcripts were analyzed using open, axial, and selective coding with a constant comparative method, leading to the identification of a core category and the development of a conceptual model. ATLAS.ti was used to manage and code the data. This study involved 26 experts (21 males and 5 females) working on health promotion interventions in a military context. Five key categories emerged as facilitators: organizational, structural, professional, collaborative, and military factors. Barriers were grouped into three categories: organizational, professional, and military factors. Key facilitators included information sharing, the proximity of health personnel at lower levels, sharing best experiences, trainings, working with a shared understanding and with partners, the chain of command, living in mass, and being young. Major barriers included resource constraints, staff turnover, the demanding nature of military work, living in mass, deployment in desert environments, and peer influence. The successful implementation of health promotion interventions in military settings is influenced by the dynamic interaction of organizational, structural, professional, collaborative, and military factors. This study identified key facilitators and barriers to health promotion interventions in the military context. The chain of command and the presence of health personnel at lower levels emerged as key facilitators, while resource constraints were important barriers. These findings, along with the conceptual model developed, provide valuable guidance for policymakers and practitioners involved in health promotion efforts within the Ethiopian military context.

title: Blind giving predicts longitudinal increases in scam susceptibility in later life
abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Financial fraud is a common and consequential threat among older adults, with estimated prevalence rates ranging from 4% to 17% annually. Although cognitive decline has been widely studied as a risk factor, less is known about behavioral characteristics that may predict changes in scam susceptibility. In the present study, we examined whether blind giving predicted trajectories of scam susceptibility across a two-year period and whether this association differed as a function of age. Research Design and Methods One hundred and sixteen cognitively unimpaired older adults (aged 51 to 83; 72% female) completed a behavioral economic measure of blind giving at baseline and a self-report measure of scam susceptibility annually across three visits. Results Linear mixed-effects models revealed a significant interaction between time, blind giving, and age (p = .022), such that greater baseline blind giving was associated with increasing scam susceptibility over time among relatively older participants, whereas scam susceptibility remained stable across levels of blind giving among relatively younger participants. Blind giving was not associated with scam susceptibility at baseline (p = .515), and the longitudinal association persisted after separately adjusting for global cognition, socioeconomic status, and race (all ps ≤ .026). Discussion and Implications Greater blind giving predicted longitudinal increases in scam susceptibility over a two-year period, with this pattern observed specifically in advanced age. These findings suggest that prosocial tendencies may become maladaptive in later life, underscoring the importance of identifying at-risk individuals to inform prevention efforts in aging populations.

title: What Does a Donor Need to Know? Content Analysis of Informed Consent Documents Used for Brain Organoid Research.
abstract: Donors of cells used to create induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and brain organoids may not understand what brain organoids are, how they will be used, or the long-term implications of the research. Informed consent documents (ICDs) often contain highly technical language and are written at reading grade levels higher than those attained by the target population. Our goal was to evaluate informed consent documents used for brain organoid research. We compared 20 currently active, IRB-approved consent documents to published templates/guidelines for iPSC research consent. Analyzed ICDs adhered to guidelines in explaining risks and benefits, de-identification, commercial potential, storage, and results sharing. However, descriptions of current and future use were lacking in detail, and the average reading level of ICDs far exceeded that of the general population. Our findings suggest additional transparency in ICDs would assist participants in making an informed choice about participation in iPSC and brain organoid research.

title: The Benefits of Prosociality towards AI Agents: Examining the Effects of Helping AI Agents on Human Well-Being
abstract: Prosocial behaviors, such as helping others, are well-known to enhance human well-being. While there is a growing trend of humans helping AI agents, it remains unclear whether the well-being benefits of helping others extend to interactions with non-human entities. To address this, we conducted an experiment (N = 295) to explore how helping AI agents impacts human well-being, especially when the agents fulfill human basic psychological needs--relatedness, competence, and autonomy--during the interaction. Our findings showed that helping AI agents reduced participants' feelings of loneliness. When AI met participants' needs for competence and autonomy during the helping process, there was a further decrease in loneliness and an increase in positive affect. However, when AI did not meet participants' need for relatedness, participants experienced an increase in positive affect. We discuss the implications of these findings for understanding how AI can support human well-being.

title: Visual-linguistic cues in manual communication: Neural and behavioral responses to Mouthings in sign-naïve perception.
abstract: Gesture serves as a foundational modality for conveying event structure, providing critical visual information about transitivity and participant roles. Sign languages integrate manual (hand-based) and non-manual (face, torso, head) articulations to encode complex linguistic information. Among these, mouth movements provide phonological and lexical cues, but their role in sign-naïve individuals remains underexplored. This study investigates how sign-naïve individuals process non-manual markers (mouthings) in unfamiliar signed verbs, to explore how linguistic information is extracted from visual stimuli sharing properties with both gesture and sign language. Using EEG, we examined whether lip-reading functions as a linguistic cue or a general perceptual enhancement in non-signers viewing Austrian Sign Language (ÖGS) and non-ÖGS stimuli. Findings reveal distinct neural signatures for manual signs presented with and without congruent mouthings. An early posterior negativity followed by a late posterior positivity suggests that mouthings facilitate lexical access by providing phonological cues that activate stored lexical representations. Conversely, stimuli without mouthings elicited increased anterior activity, reflecting heightened cognitive control demands. Further, telic verbs, which inherently encode event endpoints, showed earlier and stronger facilitation from congruent mouthings compared to atelic verbs. These findings align with the Event Visibility Hypothesis and reinforce the role of visual cues in linguistic comprehension.

title: Structured communication interventions for families of patients in the intensive care unit: A scoping review.
abstract: The aim of this study was to map structured communication interventions for families or surrogate decision-makers of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients, describe their main characteristics and reported outcomes, and organise reported intervention components into a descriptive communication-domain map. A scoping review using descriptive evidence mapping and a combined deductive-inductive synthesis of communication domains. Sources of evidence included PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), LILACS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and reference list screening. Eligibility criteria included primary studies reporting structured communication protocols, frameworks, checklists, bundles, tools, or reproductible interventions implemented by ICU clinical teams to support communication with families or surrogate decision-makers of adult ICU patients. Two reviewers independently extracted study and intervention characteristics, outcomes, measurement approaches, and quantitative findings, and reported limitations using a standardised form. Reported intervention components were charted and organised into descriptive communication domains through a combined deductive-inductive synthesis process; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Nine studies (2010-2022) were included and grouped into structured communication frameworks, educational/training interventions, and multicomponent bundles. Reported communication components were unevenly represented across included sources. Empathy/emotional support, knowledge transmission, summarisation, and value elicitation were among the most frequently described components, whereas ethical considerations, cultural adaptation, time management, nonverbal communication, and supportive aids were less frequently reported in published intervention descriptions. Outcomes were predominantly perceptual and process related. Structured ICU family communication interventions are heterogeneous in design, delivery, and outcome assessment. This review provides an evidence map of intervention types and a descriptive-domain map of reported communication components. These findings may support the development and reporting of more comprehensive, context-sensitive ICU family communication interventions.

title: Genomic structural equation modeling dissects Th2-mediated and Th2-independent genetic pathways of the atopic march.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and childhood-onset asthma (COA) share genetic susceptibility, but the contribution captured by type 2 (Th2) inflammatory traits and the residual sharing are incompletely resolved. The atopic march is one clinical trajectory rather than a universal sequence. We used genomic structural equation modeling (Genomic SEM) to examine genetic covariance among AD, COA, blood eosinophil count, and IgE-related protein abundance. A latent Th2 factor defined two model-based components, termed Th2-mediated and Th2-independent. Component GWAS, MAGMA/FOCUS, single-cell scoring, spatial mapping, Mendelian randomization (MR), and protein-QTL SMR informed candidate prioritization. Functional follow-up compared HSPA1A and HSPA1B knockdown, combined knockdown, and pharmacological IKK inhibition. Component-based analyses prioritized 121 Th2-mediated and 204 Th2-independent genes, including 71 shared genes. Alternative genetic-covariance structures provided a transparent comparison of AD-to-COA representations. MR estimates were evaluated across complementary sensitivity estimators, and HSPA1A/HSPA1B SMR associations were interpreted together with their HEIDI heterogeneity results. Lesional-skin spatial contrasts attenuated after adjustment for an epidermal marker-expression score. HSPA1B knockdown increased inflammatory outputs, with larger changes after combined HSPA1A/HSPA1B knockdown, while BMS-345541 attenuated these changes. The Th2-based genetic decomposition provides a candidate map for allergic-disease biology, including HSPA1B-associated epithelial stress responses. The framework prioritizes testable biology across inherited susceptibility and epithelial stress responses, with longitudinal mediation, complete independence from type 2 biology, and skin-to-airway propagation reserved for direct clinical and mechanistic testing.

title: Cinematic narrative transportation and prosocial tendencies in college students: a moderated mediation model
abstract: Background Narrative-based entertainment has been associated with audience members’ values and behavioral tendencies, yet the mechanisms linking cinematic narrative experiences to prosocial tendencies remain unclear. Drawing on narrative transportation theory and character identification theory, this study examined whether character identification mediates the association between cinematic narrative transportation and prosocial tendencies among college students and whether moral identity moderates the second stage of this indirect pathway. Methods A cross-sectional film-viewing survey was conducted with 1054 Chinese undergraduates ( M = 20.64 ± 1.62 years; 60.06% female). After viewing Dying to Survive , participants completed the narrative engagement scale, character identification scale, moral identity scale and prosocial behavior measure(used to assess prosocial tendencies). PROCESS Models 4 and 14, with 5,000 bootstrap samples, were used to test the mediation and moderated mediation models. Results Narrative transportation was positively correlated with prosocial tendencies ( r = 0.67, p < 0.01). Character identification partially explained the association (indirect effect = 0.012, Boot 95% CI excluding zero;2.72% of the total effect). Moral identity moderated the character identification–prosocial tendencies pathway ( b = 0.106, p = 0.009): the association was significant at moderate and high levels of moral identity ( b = 0.090 and 0.139, respectively, p < 0.001), but not at a low level ( b = 0.013, p = 0.691). The conditional indirect effects followed the same pattern (moderate: indirect effect = 0.014, 95% Boot CI [0.007, 0.023]; high: indirect effect = 0.022, 95% Boot CI [0.011, 0.034]; index of moderated mediation = 0.017, 95% Boot CI [0.005, 0.031]). Conclusion Cinematic narrative transportation was associated with college students’ prosocial tendencies partly through character identification, with moral identity serving as a moderating factor in this process. Film-based aesthetic education featuring moral growth arcs may be related to prosocial tendencies, particularly among students with higher moral identity.

title: Gene-Environment Interaction in Transgenic Rats overexpressing human DISC1: Effects of Early Social Isolation on Behavioral Domains.
abstract: Early-life social isolation (SI) is a well-established environmental stressor associated with persistent behavioral alterations relevant to psychiatric disorders. Whether SI interacts with neurodevelopmental brain abnormalities to modify behavioral vulnerability remains unclear. We investigated the effects of post-weaning SI in transgenic rats overexpressing full-length human Disrupted-in-Schizophrenia 1 (tgDISC1), a model characterized by DISC1 protein aggregation, impaired dopamine homeostasis, and abnormal neuronal migration. Male wild-type (WT) and tgDISC1 rats were housed individually or in groups from postnatal day 21 for 28 consecutive days and evaluated using behavioral tests assessing stress-coping, self-care, locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, contextual fear memory, and social behavior. SI reduced grooming behavior, shortened the latency to the first immobility episode in the forced swim test, and decreased contextual freezing regardless of genotype, whereas locomotor activity and anxiety-like behavior were unaffected. Genotype-dependent differences were observed in anxiety-related measures, showing distinct performances in the Open Field and Elevated Plus Maze tests. In the social interaction test, SI selectively altered social preference, revealing a significant gene × environment interaction, indicating that neurodevelopmental brain abnormalities specifically modulated the effects of early-life SI on social behavior. Together, these findings demonstrate that early-life SI induces selective behavioral alterations, whereas DISC1-related dysfunction selectively influences the behavioral consequences of SI in the social domain rather than conferring generalized vulnerability. These results highlight the value of multidomain behavioral phenotyping in gene × environment models and identify social behavior as a sensitive marker of DISC1-related susceptibility to early-life stress, with implications for the developmental origins of psychiatric disorders.

title: HSG-Net: A Scheduling-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Surrogate for Aviation Sensing-Data Processing Chains.
abstract: Efficient end-to-end timing evaluation is essential for the design and configuration of partitioned aviation sensing-data processing chains. Task activation, partition scheduling, message dependencies, and resource sharing jointly influence flow delay, while small variations in message arrival times may introduce substantial waiting across partition execution boundaries. Conventional reference simulation can capture these interactions but becomes computationally expensive when numerous candidate configurations must be evaluated. To address this challenge, this paper proposes HSG-Net, a scheduling-aware heterogeneous graph surrogate for predicting mean end-to-end delay from system configuration information. The proposed method represents tasks, partition windows, data flows, and hardware resources as interconnected entities, integrating explicit scheduling descriptors with heterogeneous relational dependencies. Graph message passing captures scheduling and resource interactions, while an adaptive direct-flow pathway preserves flow-local timing information and combines it with graph-derived representations for multi-scale delay prediction. On 7168 held-out test flows, the three-seed HSG-Net ensemble achieves a mean absolute error of 6.372 ms relative to reference-simulator labels, with 81.18% of predictions within a 10 ms absolute-error tolerance. Architectural comparisons demonstrate improved prediction over the evaluated direct-flow-only control, supporting the complementary use of relational context and flow-local information. Furthermore, HSG-Net also supports offline candidate screening through a validation-calibrated rule that allocates reference-simulation effort. The proposed approach provides an efficient, simulation-assisted method for timing evaluation and early-stage design-space exploration of partitioned aviation sensing-data processing architectures.

title: Measuring Compassionate Decision-Making Processes in Adolescence: Development and Pilot Validation of the Youth Compassion Measure (YCM)
abstract: This sequential mixed-methods study describes the development and pilot validation of the Youth Compassion Measure (YCM), a scenario-based assessment designed to capture compassion as a context-sensitive, developmental process in adolescence. Grounded in a five-stage model (awareness, appraisal, affect and regulation, motivation, and action), the YCM was developed using youth-informed methods. Phase 1 focus groups identified common school-based forms of distress and key contextual factors shaping compassionate responding. Phase 2 cognitive interviews refined scenarios, prompts, and coding procedures to capture adolescents’ conditional reasoning and decision processes. This article focuses on Phase 3, which evaluated construct-to-design alignment, internal coherence, and preliminary relations to theoretically relevant constructs in a sample of 200 middle school students. Open-ended and Likert-type responses were used to derive indicators across compassion components. Correlations with validated measures were modest but theoretically consistent, with stronger associations observed for intrinsic prosocial motivation and goal-directed distress tolerance. Contextual analyses indicated that relational closeness and social-evaluative conditions significantly shaped compassionate intentions and action planning. Interrater reliability for coding was high (κ = .92). Findings provide initial validity evidence for a developmentally grounded, contextually sensitive measure and highlight the importance of regulatory and motivational processes in adolescent compassionate action. Rather than representing a final measure, this study served as an important first step in the iterative development and validation of the YCM. While correlations were modest, the findings generated critical insights into the processes underlying compassionate action and highlighted opportunities to strengthen the measure, guiding the next phase of refinement and validation.

title: From movement skills to social inclusion: a systematic review of cooperative learning across activity-based learning
abstract: Introduction: Cooperative learning has increasingly been applied in physical education and other activity-based learning contexts to connect movement development with motivation, peer interaction, responsibility, and inclusion. However, the evidence had remained fragmented across educational levels, activity types, intervention designs, and outcome domains. Methodology: Scopus was searched on 13 July 2026 using a predefined Boolean strategy and eligibility criteria. Of 1,177 records initially identified, 36 unique studies published from 2017 to 2026 were included after publication-year and database restrictions, scope assessment, and eligibility screening. Because participants, activities, interventions, designs, and measures were heterogeneous, findings were synthesized narratively across four domains. Methodological quality was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and design-specific MMAT criteria. Results: Cooperative learning was associated with favorable outcomes in motor skills, academic learning time, motivation, responsibility, peer relationships, empathy, and prosocial behavior. Social-affective benefits did not consistently coincide with superior physical performance, and physical-activity outcomes varied with intervention duration, task design, habituation, and teacher support. Methodological appraisal revealed frequent concerns, especially in nonrandomized studies. Discussion: Positive interdependence, individual accountability, meaningful roles, feedback, and sustained teacher scaffolding appeared important for productive cooperation, whereas poorly structured group work could reproduce dominance, inactivity, or unequal participation. Conclusions: Cooperative learning should not be assumed to be inclusive by default; its educational value appears to depend on equitable task access, meaningful contribution, sufficient movement opportunities, explicit peer-feedback structures, and sustained implementation.

title: Wanting to matter and learning to care: A neurodevelopmental window of opportunity for (Pro) social learning?
abstract: Wanting to matter-to feel socially recognized, appreciated, and capable of actions that benefit others-represents a fundamental motivation in human development. The motivational salience of mattering appears to increase in adolescence. Evidence suggests this is related to pubertal increases in the incentive salience for gaining social value and personal agency. This can provide a useful heuristic for understanding motivational proclivities (i.e. wanting to matter) that influence action-outcome learning as young adolescents are exploring and learning how to navigate increasingly complex social and relational environments. Adolescence also brings new capacities, motives, and opportunities for learning to care about and contribute to the benefit of others. Together, these create a window of opportunity: a sensitive period for learning to gain salient feelings of mattering through caring prosocial actions and valued societal contributions. Successfully discovering ways of mattering by doing things that matter to others may contribute to formative socio-emotional learning about self/other. Advances in understanding these social and relational learning processes and their neurodevelopmental underpinnings can inform strategies to improve developmental trajectories of social competence and wellbeing among adolescents growing up in a rapidly changing and increasingly techno-centric world.

title: Bibliometric Applications in Social Science Research: The Social Network Context of Generosity
abstract: Whether or not a person chooses to act philanthropically can seem like a personal decision. Yet, giving is inherently a social act, minimally involving a giver and a receiver. The relational aspects of giving decisions can be studied by investigating social networks. What is known about the role of social networks in charitable giving? To answer this question, this study utilizes bibliometric techniques to review existing literature in a systematic manner. Applying these tools to social science research facilitates integration of knowledge across multiple disciplines and diverse methodological approaches. Across the reviewed research, there are five central themes. First, networks can shape values of efforts to support the public good. Second, networks can informally punish people for acting too self-interestedly. Third, networks can join together or exclude, contributing to social inequality and its reproduction over time. Fourth, networks can maintain group dynamics. Fifth, networks can pattern behaviors into habits, form interdependence, situate what is considered normal, and provide stability in times of crisis. Implications of existing research are drawn toward understanding young adulthood within its networked social contexts of generosity.

title: Oxytocin salvages context-specific hyperaltruistic preference through moral framing
abstract: Abstract An intriguing advancement in recent moral decision-making research suggests that people are more willing to sacrifice monetary gains to spare others from suffering than to spare themselves, yielding a hyperaltruistic tendency. Other studies, however, indicate an opposite egoistic bias in that subjects are less willing to harm themselves for the benefits of others than for their own benefits. These results highlight the delicate inner workings of moral decision and call for a mechanistic account of hyperaltruistic preference. We investigated the boundary conditions of hyperaltruism by presenting subjects with trade-off choices combing monetary gains and painful electric shocks, or, choices combing monetary losses and shocks. We first showed in study 1 that switching the decision context from gains to losses effectively eliminated the hyperaltruistic preference and the decision context effect was associated with the altered relationship between subjects’ instrumental harm (IH) trait attitudes and their relative pain sensitivities. In the pre-registered study 2, we tested whether oxytocin, a neuropeptide linked to parochial altruism, might salvage the context-dependent hyperaltruistic preference. We found that oxytocin increased subjects’ reported levels of framing the task as harming (vs. helping) others, which mediated the correlation between IH and relative pain sensitivities. Thus, the loss decision context and oxytocin nullified and restored the mediation effect of subjective harm framing, respectively. Our results help to elucidate the psychological processes underpinning the contextual specificity of hyperaltruism and carry implications in promoting prosocial interactions in our society.

title: Segment Anything Model-Guided Dual-Branch Swin Transformer with Cross-Attention Fusion for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Grading on X-ray Images.
abstract: We investigate a Segment Anything Model (SAM)-guided dual-branch Swin Transformer for knee osteoarthritis severity grading from X-ray images. A threshold-assisted SAM pipeline generates bone-region masks without task-specific SAM fine-tuning. Separate Swin-B branches process the image and mask, and two unidirectional cross-attention modules integrate their features. In the reported five-class evaluation, the model achieves 78.80\% accuracy, a macro-averaged one-vs-rest AUC of 0.9588, and quadratic weighted kappa of 0.8780. The corresponding three-class accuracy is 79.58\%. Expanded comparisons include KOA-specific methods and ablations of mask generation, weight sharing, and fusion configuration. These results support the usefulness of combining image context with mask-derived structural information within the evaluated setting.

title: Multi-Task Deep Learning for Joint Depth-Map Reconstruction and Iso-Point Prediction from Hyperspectral Images of Turbid Phantoms.
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) of turbid, tissue-mimicking media entangles the geometry of subsurface inclusions with the optical properties of the surrounding matrix in every spectrum. From HSI cubes of polyurethane phantoms with obliquely drilled inclusions we recover two physically distinct quantities: a dense depth map of the inclusion and the scalar iso-point wavelength, the point of near-invariance at which the depth-dependent modulation of the diffuse reflectance cancels. A single multi-task U-Net is a poor compromise for such complementary targets, the dense and scalar heads reaching their optima at different epochs while global pooling destroys the spectral-position information a wavelength target needs. We therefore decompose the problem into two specialised networks sharing one pipeline: a Bin Latent Transformer (BiLT) cross-attention scanner for the iso-point and a masked, zero-padded U-Net for the depth map. Under a strict cross-phantom split the depth network reaches a mean relative error of 6.07±0.71% (R2=0.934±0.014), against 19.4% for the analytic two-band index of earlier work and about 12.9% for the multi-task baseline. Zero-padding with a masked loss, preserving the inclusion-width information that cropping discards, is the decisive ingredient, and conditioning depth on the iso-point yields no further gain. The iso-point network reaches 5.03±0.93 nm RMSE (R2=0.630±0.085) from the spectra alone. Plausible settings of the iso-point detector change the labels themselves by 2.6 to 3.9 nm root-mean-square, while the retrained network stays between 4.8 and 5.3 nm. Together with oracle and per-patch-detection diagnostics, this identifies the ceiling as a detector-limited label-noise floor rather than a model deficiency. Averaging over a whole inclusion lowers the RMSE to a 3.27 nm plateau, separating an averageable random error from an irreducible regression-to-the-mean bias. For the straight, obliquely drilled bores tested here the depth task is solved to deployable accuracy, and the iso-point network gives a useful per-segment estimate where direct optical determination fails.

title: Normal Early Investigations Do Not Exclude Bickerstaff Brainstem Encephalitis: Highlighting Diagnostic and Treatment Pitfalls.
abstract: Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis (BBE) is a rare immune-mediated disorder characterized by ophthalmoplegia, cerebellar ataxia, and impaired consciousness. It is now recognized as a variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), sharing common pathogenic mechanisms with Miller Fisher syndrome. However, early diagnosis remains challenging, particularly when initial investigations are normal. We report a 20-year-old previously healthy woman presenting with rapidly progressive ophthalmoplegia, bulbar dysfunction, flaccid quadriparesis, areflexia, and impaired consciousness following a febrile upper respiratory illness. Early cerebrospinal fluid analysis and brain MRI were normal. Anti-GQ1b antibodies were positive, and nerve conduction studies showed isolated proximal conduction abnormalities with absent F-waves. The patient developed respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and was treated with an extended course of plasma exchange, resulting in near-complete recovery. This case highlights a critical diagnostic pitfall: BBE, a variant of GBS, can present with a life-threatening brainstem syndrome despite entirely normal early investigations. We emphasize the value of recognizing the paradoxical combination of areflexia and extensor plantar responses and the use of F-wave studies as an early electrophysiological foothold when standard studies are unrevealing. Furthermore, it demonstrates that even in catastrophic, ventilator-dependent presentations, an extended course of plasma exchange can lead to a favorable outcome, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for severe presentations of BBE.

title: Al Decoration versus Al Substitution in MnO2 Monolayers: Strategy-Dependent Interfacial Mechanisms for NO2 Capture and Sensing.
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a hazardous atmospheric pollutant, making its efficient adsorption and sensitive detection important for environmental monitoring and pollution control. Pristine MnO2 monolayers, however, generally show weak interfacial interactions and limited charge transfer during NO2 adsorption, which restricts their adsorption and sensing performance. Herein, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to elucidate how two Al modification strategies, namely surface decoration (Al-decorated) and substitutional doping (Al-substituted), regulate NO2 adsorption on MnO2 monolayers. Particular attention was paid to the relationship among modification strategy, interfacial bonding mechanism, and application tendency. H-site Al-decorated MnO2 (H-Al-MnO2) and T2-site Al-substituted MnO2 (T2-Al-MnO2) were identified as the most stable configurations. Although both Al modification strategies substantially strengthen the interaction with NO2, with adsorption energies of -3.689 and -1.133 eV and charge transfers of -0.62 and +0.34 e, respectively, they induce distinct interfacial bonding modes. In H-Al-MnO2, dual-site O-Al interactions promote charge separation and electrostatic attraction, giving rise to a predominantly ionic interface. In contrast, T2-Al-MnO2 favors a single N-O interaction characterized by electron sharing and orbital hybridization, resulting in a more evident covalent component. These strategy-dependent interfacial bonding mechanisms lead to distinct functional tendencies. H-Al-MnO2 is more suitable for NO2 capture owing to strong adsorption, difficult desorption, and preferential NO2 adsorption, whereas T2-Al-MnO2 is more promising for reusable NO2 sensing owing to its moderate adsorption strength, high sensitivity, favorable recovery behavior, and good NO2 selectivity. This work establishes a structure-mechanism-performance relationship in Al-modified MnO2 monolayers, revealing how modification strategy governs interfacial bonding and drives distinct NO2 capture and sensing tendencies.

title: Layered Uranyl Hydroxide Assembled from Negatively Charged Host Layers and Interlayer Cations through Noncovalent Interactions.
abstract: Uranyl oxide hydroxide phases have attracted sustained attention due to their critical role in the disposal and remediation of radioactive waste. The variety of layered uranyl hydroxides (LUHs) remains limited; only four neutral LUH phases have been structurally confirmed. Herein, we report the synthesis and characterization of the first charged LUH, [BMIM]2[(UO2)5(OH)12(H2O)2] (BMIM-UOH), which represents the fifth confirmed LUH phase. In BMIM-UOH, pentagonal-bipyramidal uranyl units are interconnected to vertex-sharing [(UO2)5(μ2-OH)12] ({U5}) clusters, which further link to form extended two-dimensional anionic sheets, with ionic liquid cations serving as interlayer counterions. The resulting uranyl hydroxide layer exhibits a new anion topology that has not been observed in other uranyl compounds. Notably, the ionic liquid cations occupy the interlayer galleries, where they stabilize the layered structures through electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonding. This structure represents a rare example of LUHs, highlighting the role of ionic liquids in modulating actinyl hydrolysis and assembling layered materials.

title: Whole-Ventricle Cardiac Cine MRI in a Single Breath-Hold With Slice- and Time-Dependent Deep Image Prior at 0.55T.
abstract: To develop a whole-ventricle cardiac cine MRI radial acquisition at 0.55T in a single breath-hold scan of approximately 12-15 s, reconstructed using a novel self-supervised slice and time-dependent deep image prior (ST-DIP) neural network. A whole-ventricle cardiac cine MRI at 0.55T is acquired in a single breath-hold by collecting eight slices (1.5 s per slice) and reconstructing them jointly using ST-DIP. Acquisition uses a tiny golden angle radial trajectory and a balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) readout. Reconstruction uses a frequency-weighted consistency loss in the frequency domain and total variation regularization in the image domain, sharing the same network weights for all slices. The proposed approach was tested in 10 healthy subjects and was compared with time-dependent deep image prior (TD-DIP) and conventional reconstruction methods. ST-DIP achieves an edge sharpness of ST-DIP enables whole-ventricle cine imaging in a single breath-hold and reconstruction of high-quality cine images at 0.55T, outperforming conventional methods in image quality while providing comparable LVEF to a 15-s-per-slice radial reference cine scan.

title: Facet joint fusion in lumbar surgery: a biomechanical review of posterior column preservation and reconstruction.
abstract: Adjacent segment disease (ASD) is a multifactorial long-term complication of lumbar interbody fusion. In addition to patient-related factors, pre-existing degeneration, sagittal alignment, and fusion-related changes in construct stiffness, iatrogenic disruption of the posterior elements may contribute to altered adjacent-segment biomechanics. The role of the facet joint complex in this process has received comparatively limited attention. This narrative review synthesizes biomechanical, cadaveric, and clinical evidence concerning lumbar facet arthrodesis, posterior-column preservation and reconstruction, and two-column fixation after lumbar interbody fusion. Biomechanical studies suggest that preservation of the posterior ligamentous and facet structures can influence segmental stability, load sharing, and adjacent-level intradiscal or facet stresses. Facet-based fixation provides rotational constraint under experimental conditions and may offer a different stiffness profile from conventional pedicle screw constructs. The potential role of facet arthrodesis appears to depend on the extent of posterior-element disruption, residual instability, and the stability requirements of the overall construct. Current evidence is insufficient to recommend its routine use after TLIF or PLIF or to conclude that it reduces symptomatic ASD, reoperation rates, or improves long-term patient-reported outcomes. Prospective clinical studies with long-term follow-up are required.

title: Biological, genomic, and biogeographic characterization of two lytic phages infecting Vibrio natriegens.
abstract: Vibrio natriegens is a marine bacterium known for its exceptionally rapid growth and has recently attracted considerable attention as an alternative host microorganism in the field of biotechnology. Despite this growing interest, phages infecting this species remain poorly characterized. In this study, two lytic phages that infect V. natriegens, vB_Vna_AM1 and vB_Vna_AM2, were isolated and subjected to biological characterization and phylogenetic analysis. Phages vB_Vna_AM1 and vB_Vna_AM2 were isolated from the Sumiyō River mangrove area in Amamigunto National Park, Kagoshima, Japan. Their morphology was determined using transmission electron microscopy. One-step growth curve experiments, host-range evaluation, and viability tests under different temperature, salinity, and pH conditions were performed. Whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and homology searches against global ocean virome datasets were conducted. vB_Vna_AM1 and vB_Vna_AM2 exhibited prolate capsids and contractile tails, with latent periods of 40-60 min, and both infected V. natriegens specifically among the tested strains. Their genome sizes and GC contents were 244,321 bp and 41.51% for vB_Vna_AM1, and 327,464 bp and 40.67% for vB_Vna_AM2, respectively. Both phages were assigned to a subcluster of other vibriophages, showing similarities of 92.1-92.2% for vB_Vna_AM1 and 86.8-86.9% for vB_Vna_AM2. Homology searches using global ocean virome datasets revealed that homologous genes were distributed globally at the protein level; however, they were detected as partial genes within otherwise diverse viral genomes. This study provides the initial description and phylogenetic analysis of newly isolated phages infecting V. natriegens. These findings expand the currently limited repertoire of culturable phages of V. natriegens and support the concept that gene modules may be shared among diverse phages within a gene-sharing network, contributing to the understanding of marine viral diversity.

title: Empathy and perspective-taking in literary fiction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of psychological evidence and theoretical insights
abstract: Background It has been argued over the years that fiction reading can be useful in making people know other people, but the empirical history is spotty and frequently contradictory. Investigations vary in their design, measurements and quality and there is still no clear vision of how powerful those effects are and in what circumstances they manifest themselves. Methods A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and ERIC of studies published within the past 20 years (2000–2025) that investigated literary or prosocial reading relative to empathy, perspective-taking, theory of mind, or prosocial behaviour. Twenty-one studies were eligible. Of these, 12 contributed enough statistical information to be included in the meta-analysis, yielding 14 independent effect sizes (standardized mean differences and correlations, transformed to Hedges’ g and Fisher’s z ). Random-effects models were used, and heterogeneity and potential publication bias was examined with standard tests. Results When all eligible outcomes were pooled, reading literary or prosocial texts was associated with a small but statistically reliable advantage in social-cognitive performance (overall g = 0.23, 95% CI [0.11, 0.35], z = 3.78, p < 0.001). For cognitive empathy and theory of mind specifically, experimental studies produced a pooled effect of g = 0.27, 95% CI [0.10, 0.44], z = 3.15, p = 0.002 and correlational work showed an association of r = 0.20, 95% CI [0.03, 0.36], z = 4.75, p < 0.001. Across the 21 primary studies, 10 (47.6%) reported positive or beneficial outcomes, 6 (28.6%) reported mediated or conditional effects, 5 (23.8%) reported null or weak effects, and 3 (14.3%) contributed neurocognitive evidence. Because these evidence descriptors were not mutually exclusive, percentages were not intended to form a partition of the study set. Conclusion Taken together, the findings suggest that reading literary fiction does not uniformly transform readers’ empathy, but is linked to modest, context-sensitive gains, particularly in perspective-taking and theory of mind. These gains are most visible when readers are engaged with demanding narratives and are invited, by the text or by instructions, to actively simulate characters’ minds, with affective empathy and prosocial responses emerging more selectively under such conditions.
